# kenilworthford-website

The [kenilworthford.com](https://kenilworthford.com) website, which shows whether the Kenilworth ford is flooded, using river levels from the [river-levels](https://github.com/daveshepherd/river-levels) API.

The site is built with webpack from [`site/`](site). The CDK app in [`src/`](src) uploads each release to its own folder in S3, `/<version>/`, and CloudFront serves the active release at the site root.

See [docs/infrastructure.md](docs/infrastructure.md) for the architecture, releases, testing and rollback.

## Getting Started

Prerequisites:
* Node.js 26
* Yarn 1 (classic)
* AWS credentials for the target account, needed to deploy

```sh
yarn install
npx projen build
```

## CDK

Bootstrap each AWS account and region once:

```sh
npx cdk bootstrap
```

Deploy the app:

```sh
npx projen deploy
```

This deploys every stack in the app. To deploy a single stack, name it, as in `npx cdk deploy <stack>`.

## Deployment

After each release, the release workflow deploys to these GitHub environments in order, each after the previous one succeeds:

| Environment | Region | Secrets |
| ----------- | ------ | ------- |
| development | eu-west-2 | `AWS_DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN` |
| production | eu-west-2 | `AWS_DEPLOYMENT_ROLE_ARN` |

Each environment needs these secrets set, the first being the ARN of a role that trusts GitHub's OIDC provider.

## Contributing

Pull request titles must follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org), with one of the types `feat`, `fix` or `chore`, such as `feat: describe the change`. The **Validate PR title** check fails until the title does.

Once a pull request is approved, or is opened by `daveshepherd`, and its checks pass, the [Mergify](https://mergify.com) merge queue squash merges it, with its title as the commit message. Draft pull requests and those labelled `do-not-merge` are not merged.

The type decides the next release: `feat` releases a minor version and `fix` a patch version, while a breaking change, marked by `!` after the type (such as `feat!: ...`) or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer, releases a major version. Other types still release a patch version.
